shots.say: Why does Tumble have such big ears?
Are they for flying? Or for keeping cool?
I'm Milo. Let's find out together!
Welcome to The Animated Zoo, friends!
Today we fly to the sunny savanna.
Here we are! Look who is waiting for us.
This is Tumble. Tumble is a baby elephant.
And this is Tumble's mama. Hello, Mama!
Look at Mama's ears. They are so, so big!
African elephants have very large ears.
Where are your ears? Can you touch your ears?
Mama's ear is much bigger than me!
Let's count birds up the ear. One, two, three! Still more ear!
And look at the shape. Can you see it?
It looks like a map of Africa!
African elephants have ears shaped like Africa.
Asian elephants live far away. They have smaller ears.
Which one has bigger ears? This one, or that one?
This one! The African elephant, like Mama and Tumble.
Tumble's ears are big, and they can move. Flap, flap!
Tumble's ears are big. But Mama's ears are even bigger!
Who has bigger ears, Tumble or Mama?
Mama! She is big, and her ears are big too.
Can Tumble fly with his big ears? He tries. Flap, flap, jump!
Bump! No. Elephants cannot fly.
Big ears are not wings.
Can you flap your hands like big ears? Flap, flap, flap!
So what are big ears for? Let's find out!
Phew! The sun is hot on the savanna.
Tumble feels hot, hot, hot.
Watch Mama. She flaps her big ears. Flap, flap, flap!
Tumble flaps his ears, too. Ahh, that feels nice.
Tumble walks into the green jungle. It is still so hot!
Flap, flap, flap! His ears make a little wind.
How many ears does Tumble have? One, or two?
Two! Two big ears to flap.
Big ears flap like a fan on a hot day. Whoosh, whoosh!
An elephant's ears help it stay cool.
When an elephant flaps its ears, the ears cool down.
And that cools the whole big body.
Do big ears help an elephant keep warm, or keep cool?
Keep cool! Flap, flap, cool.
Can you fan your face with your hands? Ahh, nice and cool!
On warm days, elephants flap their ears a lot.
Let's count Tumble's flaps. One, two, three!
Mama flaps her ears slowly. Flap... flap... flap.
Tumble and Mama rest in the shade of the big tree.
Now they feel cool. Big ears, big job!
That is one way to keep cool. One, flap your ears.
Tumble and Mama walk to the cool river.
Time for a cool drink. Watch Mama's trunk!
She sucks the water part way up her trunk. Slurp!
Only part of the way up. Not all the way!
Then she curls her trunk to her mouth,
and the water pours in. Glug, glug, glug.
Does Mama drink with her trunk, or with her tail?
With her trunk! Ahh, a cool drink.
Tumble has a cool drink, too. Slurp, slurp!
Two, have a drink.
And now? Tumble walks into the deep water.
Can elephants swim? Yes, or no?
Elephants can swim! They swim to cool off, and to play.
Splash, splash! Tumble swims along. Bubble, bubble!
Can you swim with your arms? Splash, splash, splash!
Out he comes, all wet and cool. Drip, drip!
Flap, flap, flap! Tumble feels nice and cool.
Three, go for a swim!
Which way do you like best? Flap, drink, or swim?
The sun goes down. Tumble walks home with Mama.
Tumble flaps his ears one more time. Cool and happy!
Big ears, big job. Wow!
Time to remember what we learned!
Can an elephant fly with its ears? Yes, or no?
No! Big ears are not wings.
What do big ears help an elephant do? Keep cool, or keep warm?
Keep cool! Flap, flap, cool.
And what shape is an African elephant's ear?
Like Africa!
Three ways to keep cool. Let's say them!
Flap, drink, swim!
Good night, Tumble. Good night, Mama.
Thank you for learning with me, friends. See you at the zoo!
